title: Standardized Protocol for Extracting and Quantifying PLFA and NLFA Biomarkers from Soil
author: Simone Cesarz
materials: After removal, add 2.0 ml hexane-chloroform solution.
Freeze the vials at -20 °C upon measurement.

steps.title: Label tubes and blanks
steps.instruction: Label two sets of twelve 50 ml glass centrifuge tubes; include two blanks (no soil, only reagents) with one blank placed at the beginning and one at the end of the sequence.

steps.title: Weigh soil sample
steps.instruction: Weigh 5 ± 0.1 g fresh soil into each labeled tube, record the exact fresh weight and the empty‑tube weight for later dry‑weight normalization.

steps.title: First Bligh‑Dyer extraction
steps.instruction: Add 18.5 ml Bligh‑Dyer solvent to each tube, vortex 1 min, shake on an overhead shaker at 30 rpm for 1 h, vortex 1 min, and shake again at 30 rpm for 1 h.

steps.title: First centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 1500 g for 10 min at 8 °C to pellet soil debris.

steps.title: Transfer first supernatant
steps.instruction: Using glass Pasteur pipettes, transfer the supernatant to new 50 ml glass tubes (label the 12 tubes).

steps.title: Second solvent extraction
steps.instruction: Add a further 5 ml Bligh‑Dyer to the soil residue, vortex for 5 min.

steps.title: Second centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge again under the same conditions (1500 g, 10 min, 8 °C).

steps.title: Transfer second supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer the second supernatant to the same new 50 ml tube used in step 4.

steps.title: Dry soil residue
steps.instruction: Dry the remaining soil residue overnight under a fume hood, then at 105 °C to obtain dry weight for normalization.

steps.title: Phase‑separation addition
steps.instruction: To the pooled supernatants add 6.2 ml chloroform and 6.2 ml citrate buffer, vortex 5 min to separate aqueous and organic phases.

steps.title: Phase‑separation centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge as before; beginners should centrifuge the first six 50 ml tubes first and the remaining six later to avoid mixing of phases.

steps.title: Prepare Na₂SO₄ filtration columns
steps.instruction: Fill glass Pasteur pipettes with glass wool, add ~1 cm water‑free Na₂SO₄, and build adapters from 2 ml reaction tubes and pipette tips so the columns rest on the tube rim, not inside the tube.

steps.title: Filter lower organic phase
steps.instruction: Using a short Pasteur pipette, push through both phases while gently expelling air, then draw the lower (organic) phase with a long Pasteur pipette; transfer ≥5 ml onto the Na₂SO₄ column, allowing liquid to seep into a new 10 ml centrifuge tube without the fill level reaching the adapters.

steps.title: Collect full‑milliliter fractions
steps.instruction: Transfer only full milliliters (usually 7 ml) to the prepared 10 ml tubes and record the exact volume for each sample.

steps.title: Optional overnight stop
steps.instruction: Samples may be frozen at –20 °C at this point; otherwise continue with step 16.

steps.title: Evaporate organic phase
steps.instruction: Evaporate the organic phase under a nitrogen stream at 35 °C, monitoring the liquid level, lowering the jet height as needed, and stopping when completely dry; immediately close tubes and turn off the N₂ supply.

steps.title: Set up vacuum manifold
steps.instruction: Under a fume hood, set up the vacuum manifold, connect the pump, and mount Si‑columns.

steps.title: Condition Si‑columns
steps.instruction: Close column valves, place solvent waste beakers under the needles, add 2 ml chloroform to each Si‑column, open valves to wet the columns, keep columns wet (never let them dry), and close valves before the chloroform reaches the Si‑layer.

steps.title: Label fraction tubes
steps.instruction: Label two sets of 10 ml centrifuge tubes: “Chl” for the NLFA (chloroform) fraction and “Me” for the PLFA (methanol) fraction (e.g., Chl1, Chl2 …; Me1, Me2 …).

steps.title: Replace waste beakers with NLFA tubes
steps.instruction: After evaporation, replace the solvent‑waste beakers with the previously labeled NLFA tubes (Chl1, Chl2 …).

steps.title: Redissolve extract and load onto columns
steps.instruction: Redissolve each evaporated extract with 300 µl chloroform, shake gently, load onto the Si‑columns with a pipette, then add 2.0 ml chloroform to each column (pay attention to the order of NLFA tubes).

steps.title: Vacuum‑draw solvent
steps.instruction: Apply low‑pressure vacuum (under the hood, exhaust directed away) to suck solvent through the columns; observe all columns simultaneously and close their valves before the solvent meniscus reaches the column material.

steps.title: Add additional chloroform
steps.instruction: Repeat the solvent‑addition step with a further 2.5 ml chloroform per column.

steps.title: Flush columns with acetone
steps.instruction: Flush each column with six × 2.0 ml acetone; discard the acetone waste.

steps.title: Collect PLFA fraction
steps.instruction: Replace the waste containers with a rack of new tubes labeled “Me” and add 2 × 2.5 ml methanol to each column to elute the PLFA fraction.

steps.title: Prepare drying oven
steps.instruction: Set the drying oven to 37 °C and place a metal evaporation‑block rack inside.

steps.title: Evaporate fraction under N₂
steps.instruction: Evaporate the NLFA or PLFA phase at 35 °C under a nitrogen atmosphere (beginners may process only one phase at a time); during this step freshly prepare methanolic KOH for the upcoming methylation.

steps.title: Add internal standard
steps.instruction: Add 30 µl of internal standard (C19:0, methylnonadecanoate) to the dry extract at the bottom of the tube using a high‑accuracy pipette.

steps.title: Add methanol‑toluene solution
steps.instruction: Add 1.0 ml methanol‑toluene solution and vortex for 1 min.

steps.title: Add methanolic KOH
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml freshly prepared methanolic KOH, close the tube carefully, and vortex for 1 min.

steps.title: Heat for methylation
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in the drying oven for 15 min.

steps.title: Neutralize reaction
steps.instruction: Add 0.3 ml acetic acid followed by 2 ml deionized water, then vortex for 5 min.

steps.title: Separate phases
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the samples (same conditions as before).

steps.title: Collect upper organic phase
steps.instruction: Transfer the upper phase to new 10 ml centrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Extract remaining lower phase
steps.instruction: Add 2.0 ml hexane‑chloroform solution to the remaining lower phase, vortex 5 min, centrifuge again, and transfer the new upper phase to the tube.

steps.title: Repeat for second fraction
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 27–35 (internal standard addition through phase separation) with the second fraction (PLFA or NLFA).

steps.title: Optional overnight stop
steps.instruction: Samples may be frozen at –20 °C at this point; otherwise continue with step 38.

steps.title: Final evaporation and labeling
steps.instruction: Evaporate the final extracts at 35 °C under N₂; during evaporation insert micro‑inserts into vials and label each vial with (1) fraction, (2) sample name, and (3) running number.

steps.title: Add hexane and dilute
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl hexane to each sample, gently shake briefly, and dilute the extract by repeated careful pipetting until the whole extract is dissolved.

steps.title: Transfer to final vials
steps.instruction: Transfer the dissolved extract into the vials containing the micro‑inserts, then close the vials with plastic caps and septa.
